title: Urban Appraisal: Physiological Recording during Rating of Different Urban Environments
description: This dataset contains continuous EEG, ECG and electrodermal activity (EDA) recordings from 63 participants who viewed and rated 56 Streetview images of urban environments. Each image was rated on nine subjective scales (arousal, valence, dominance, stress, openness, safety, beauty, hominess, fascination). The data support investigation of how urban environments and their visual elements influence appraisals and neural responses, including stimulus-onset ERPs.
methods_description: 64-channel wet-electrode EEG (10-20 system, FCz reference) plus ECG and EDA were recorded at 500 Hz with BrainAmp DC amplifiers (BrainProducts). Participants sat in front of a 27-inch monitor and, using Psychtoolbox in MATLAB, viewed 56 Streetview images (3000 ms each) after a word-pair prime and fixation cross. They then rated each image on nine scales, giving 504 trials across two blocks separated by a break. Eyes-open baseline recordings of 3 min were taken at the start and end of the experiment.
